tasks.short: Pull AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube data into Excel, build tables and charts, write commentary, send to managers.

steps.what: Take the report request and agree scope, period and audience
Export data from AFAS, Recruitee, Studytube and agency portals
Clean, join and calculate metrics in Excel
Build charts and write the commentary on changes

loop.input: metric table with month-on-month deltas and metric definitions
loop.output: short narrative per section in Dutch, every number referenced to a cell
loop.check: script verifies every number in the text matches the metric table; groups under 5 people are suppressed before the model sees them
loop.stop: one draft plus one retry on a failed number check; otherwise section left blank for the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: the charts are deterministic, but explaining why verzuim or 90-day retention moved needs written prose

steps.what: Check numbers and send to HR director, HRBPs and site managers

tasks.design: Replace the Excel workbooks with a scheduled extract from AFAS GetConnectors, Recruitee and Studytube APIs into one governed Power BI semantic model with fixed metric definitions. Standard reports become Power BI paginated reports with subscriptions; a bounded model step drafts the commentary from the delta table, and the analyst approves before release. Custom requests are built on the same model, not from fresh exports.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each source needed its own export and the joins (employee to vacancy to course) lived in the analyst's Excel; building and maintaining connectors cost more time than the monthly manual work.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding makes the connector and transformation code a matter of days, and a model can draft the commentary that used to need the analyst for every report.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition of hire, productive and 90-day retention across sites and flex workers; the reasons behind a trend still need someone who knows the sites.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which change matters to the HR director this month, and what a number means given a reorganisation in Venlo or a peak season, stays with the analyst.

ambition.what: A weekly instead of monthly 90-day retention and onboarding-week-one report per site, so HRBPs act on new hires still in their first month.

tasks.altitude: The analyst stops assembling reports and spends that time on checking definitions and on the questions behind the numbers; they decide which metrics enter the standard pack.

reach.learn: How FP&A ties headcount and flex hours to the cost forecast, so HR and finance numbers match.

reach.task: Quarterly business review with site managers
reach.learn: Which questions managers actually ask, to shape the standard report.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI summarises reports on a prepared semantic model on Fabric F2+ or Premium capacity, and misreads data without one.
Standard reports fit deterministic software plus a model-drafted narrative.
Absence data is health data under GDPR Art. 9; report rates and durations, never causes.

assumptions: AFAS GetConnectors are available for the needed tables.
The company has or will buy Power BI Premium or Fabric capacity.
About 60% of report time goes to recurring reports.
unknowns: How many reports are recurring versus one-off requests.
Whether the existing Power BI AFAS extract can be extended or must be rebuilt.
Whether the works council has already consented to the current HR dashboards.
research_questions: Of the last 50 report requests, how many could have been answered from a single semantic model?
Do managers read Dutch commentary written by a model without complaints about accuracy over a three-month pilot?
Can Recruitee and Studytube APIs deliver the fields needed to join candidate, hire and course records?

tasks.short: Check nightly refresh, chase late data, send reports and manage who sees which dashboard.

steps.what: Check that the nightly AFAS extract and Power BI refresh succeeded
Chase missing or late data with HR admin and agencies
Send reports and extracts to managers by mail or Teams
Grant or remove dashboard access when managers join, move or leave
Tell users about delays and changes to reports

tasks.design: A scheduled job checks the extract and refresh each morning, runs data checks (missing end dates, open sick reports, unknown cost centres) and posts failures to a Teams channel and a status banner on the dashboards. Power BI subscriptions replace mailed reports, and row-level security is driven by the AFAS manager hierarchy, with a daily diff of access changes the analyst approves.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access lists and mail lists were kept by hand because linking AFAS org changes to Power BI roles needed scripting nobody had time for.
tasks.enabler_now: Power BI subscriptions and row-level security are standard, and AI coding makes the AFAS-to-security-role sync a small job.
tasks.still_hard: The AFAS manager hierarchy is often out of date after reorganisations, and flex workers from agencies are not in AFAS at all.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding who may see per-person absence and pay data, and handling exceptions such as an interim site manager, stays with the analyst and HR director.

ambition.what: Shift leaders on the three warehouse floors get a team view of week-one onboarding and course certificates (forklift, VCA) for the first time.

tasks.altitude: The analyst no longer sends files; they own the access rules and the data checks, and approve access changes once a day.

reach.task: Processing org and contract mutations in AFAS
reach.learn: Which mutations break reporting and how to enter them so the hierarchy stays correct.
Which expiry warnings shift leaders need and how early.

evidence.claim: Works council consent is needed for systems able to observe behaviour or performance; dashboards with per-person rows qualify.
Row-level security and minimum group sizes are the expected pattern for manager access to HR data.
Data quality checks such as missing end dates and open sick reports suit deterministic code.

assumptions: The AFAS manager hierarchy is complete enough to drive security roles.
Managers have Power BI licences or access through an app workspace.
unknowns: How many people currently receive HR reports by mail.
Whether shift leaders have Microsoft 365 accounts.
Current works council position on team-level certificate views.
research_questions: How often over the last six months did the nightly refresh fail or arrive late, and how was it noticed?
What share of AFAS employees have a correct manager field today?
Will the works council consent to team-level views for shift leaders with a minimum group size of five?

tasks.short: Change the AFAS extract, Power BI model and dashboards when definitions, sites or CAO rules change.

steps.what: Take and clarify a change request for a metric or dashboard
Change extract queries, Power Query steps and DAX measures

loop.input: change spec, current model definition and measure catalogue
loop.output: proposed SQL, Power Query and DAX changes in version control
loop.check: automated tests compare key metrics with last month's signed-off numbers; analyst reviews the diff
loop.stop: three attempts; then the analyst writes it
loop.why_not_simpler: the change is new code each time; a coding assistant drafts it, deterministic tests check it

steps.what: Test new numbers against known figures and AFAS screens
Update metric definitions and documentation

loop.check: analyst approves; definition stored next to the measure
loop.why_not_simpler: definitions must be readable prose for managers, generated from code

steps.what: Publish the change and tell users

tasks.design: Put the AFAS extract, Power Query and the semantic model in version control with a test set of signed-off monthly numbers; changes are drafted with a coding assistant and Copilot DAX help, tested automatically, then deployed through Power BI deployment pipelines. The definitions catalogue is generated from the model and published on SharePoint.
tasks.previous_blocker: Power BI models were edited by hand in the desktop tool with no tests, so every change needed a long manual check against AFAS.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistants write DAX, SQL and test scripts quickly, and Power BI supports deployment pipelines and text-based model files.
tasks.still_hard: Getting HR to agree on definitions, and legacy AFAS fields filled differently per site.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing the definition (does a flex worker who is converted count as a hire?) and judging whether a new measure is lawful and fair stays with the analyst.

ambition.what: A published HR metric catalogue that FP&A, payroll and HRBPs use as the single source for headcount, verzuim and 90-day retention.

tasks.altitude: The analyst moves from editing dashboards to owning the metric layer: definitions, tests and releases, with sign-off rights on any metric change.

reach.task: Month-end close checks on headcount and personnel cost
reach.learn: How finance reconciles FTE to the ledger, to reuse its checks.
Which AFAS fields change at close and when the extract can safely run.

evidence.claim: Copilot in Power BI writes DAX on a semantic model.
Text-to-SQL cut query writing from about 10 to 3 minutes at Uber; hallucinated tables and columns remain.

assumptions: The analyst can use a code repository and a coding assistant under company policy.
Signed-off monthly numbers exist to use as test fixtures.
unknowns: How many change requests arrive per month.
Whether Power BI deployment pipelines are licensed.
Whether IT allows a code repository for HR data models.
research_questions: How long do the last ten dashboard changes take with and without a coding assistant plus tests?
How many past errors in HR reports came from a model change that was not tested?
Do HRBPs and FP&A accept one shared definition of headcount and 90-day retention?

tasks.short: Answer manager questions about HR dashboards, fix access or filters, explain numbers that look wrong.

steps.what: Receive a question or complaint about a report
Diagnose: access, filter, data lag, definition or real data error

loop.input: question text, user's role and access, refresh status, metric definitions
loop.output: category and draft answer citing a definition or verified answer
loop.check: answers only from the verified-answer list and definitions; numbers come from the semantic model under the user's own row-level security; groups under 5 refused
loop.stop: one pass; low confidence or no verified answer routes to the analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: questions come in free Dutch text and must be matched to a definition or cause

steps.what: Explain the answer to the manager

loop.output: reply in Teams, labelled as AI
loop.check: routine answers sent from verified list; new answers held for analyst review
loop.why_not_simpler: replies must be written for the specific question

steps.what: Fix the data, access or report, or ask HR admin to correct AFAS
Note recurring questions to improve reports

tasks.design: A Teams answer desk, read-only on the HR semantic model, answers from a list of verified answers and the metric catalogue, under each manager's row-level security with a minimum group size, and says it is AI. It checks refresh status and access first, routes everything it cannot answer to the analyst, and logs every question to a dashboard that drives report fixes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrived in free text and most needed a look at access, refresh and definitions together, which only the analyst could combine.
tasks.enabler_now: Models now read Dutch free text well enough to classify a question and match it to a definition, and Copilot in Power BI can answer on a prepared model.
tasks.still_hard: Copilot in Power BI does not officially support non-English chat, and wrong answers about absence or pay harm trust quickly; verified answers take ongoing upkeep.
tasks.human_edge: Questions that hide a people problem (a manager asking about one employee's absence) need the analyst's judgment and a redirect to the HRBP.

ambition.what: Site and shift managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get answers on headcount, flex hours and verzuim rates within minutes, outside office hours.

tasks.altitude: The analyst handles only escalations and keeps the verified answer list; they decide which questions the desk may answer.

reach.task: Advising managers on absence cases under Wet verbetering poortwachter
reach.learn: Where data questions turn into case questions, to set the escalation rules.

reach.task: Reporting vacancy pipeline to hiring managers
reach.learn: The recurring hiring questions managers ask, to add verified answers.

evidence.claim: Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent answers managers on staffing; Microsoft warns faster access does not by itself mean better decisions.
Visier Vee answers people questions in Teams; no customer result named.
Copilot in Power BI non-English chat is not officially supported.
Chatbots must disclose they are AI under EU AI Act Art. 50.

assumptions: Most support questions repeat and can be covered by 30 to 60 verified answers.
unknowns: Volume and mix of support questions per month.
Whether Fabric capacity is available for Copilot.
Works council position on a chat tool over HR data.
research_questions: Of the last 100 support questions, what share was access, refresh, definition or real data error?
In a pilot, what share of Dutch questions does the desk answer correctly from verified answers?
Does a minimum group size of five block the questions site managers most need answered?

role.altitude: The analyst moves from building and sending reports to owning the HR metric layer: definitions, tests, access rules, data checks and the verified answers that managers and tools query.
reach: FP&A: align headcount and flex-hour figures with the cost forecast
HR admin: AFAS mutation quality that drives reporting and access
HRBP: escalation rules for questions that become absence or people cases
L&D: certificate expiry views for shift leaders
skills_to_grow: Version-controlled semantic models and automated data tests
Writing and maintaining verified answers and metric definitions
GDPR Art. 9 and works council (WOR 27) requirements for HR analytics
role.ambitious_version: A governed HR metric layer on Power BI that gives every site and shift manager correct, consented answers on hiring, 90-day retention, verzuim rates and certificates within a day of the data changing, with the analyst spending most of the week on what the numbers mean for the North Star.
